div.div:
The user
isAutoCreation builds a ZITADEL user from the
Google profile on first login. That is the ONLY
way a human user is created — no script can
seed one, which is why a database restore
matters more than it looks.

div.div:
Project: platform
Holds every OIDC client and the four roles:
admin · backend · frontend · data
Roles are created by zitadel-oidc-clients.sh.
Granting one to a user stays manual — the
user only exists after a first login.

div.div:
Action: flatRoles
ZITADEL has no groups — only project roles,
emitted as a nested object. This Action flattens
them and sets two claims with one list:
groups → Headlamp, Flux UI
roles → Grafana

div.div: projectRoleAssertion must be true — ZITADEL defaults it to false. With it off, no token carries roles AND ctx.v1.user.grants is empty inside the Action, so flatRoles returns early and sets no claim at all — while still logging "action run succeeded". One flag, three unrelated-looking failures: "no such key: groups" in the Flux UI, "unauthorized" in Headlamp, and every Grafana user silently landing on Viewer.

div.div:
A ZITADEL token is a Kubernetes identity. The groups claim becomes real Kubernetes groups, and rbac/admin.yaml binds the admin group to cluster-admin. Headlamp simply forwards the user's token.
Pin the PROJECT id, not one client id: the project id is in every token the project issues, so a new consumer needs no change. Pinning one app's client id silently rejects all the others — and an EKS provider config is immutable, so fixing it means ~20 minutes of downtime.

div.div:
oauth2-proxy
Authenticates the human against ZITADEL and
gates on --allowed-group=admin. Headlamp then
talks to the API server as its OWN ServiceAccount.

div.div:
GKE's managed control plane accepts no equivalent flag. Identity Service for GKE, which used to provide one, is deprecated as of 2026-07-01 and unsupported in 1.37+. Workforce Identity Federation authenticates a client to Google and cannot take a ZITADEL id_token.
The trade is explicit: per-user Kubernetes RBAC is lost, and authorisation moves entirely to the proxy. See ADR-0026 for the alternatives weighed, Pinniped included.
